key_insight: CEDAR, an evidence-citing, self-auditing LLM pipeline, outperformed trained machine-learning comparators in predicting pediatric diabetes outcomes, with the largest gains on sparsely screened outcomes.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support risk assessment from complex pediatric diabetes records, but the reported results do not establish readiness for clinical use.
method: Analyzed records from 2,489 youth with type 2 diabetes and 4,018 with type 1 diabetes.
Combined structured data and note-derived social determinants, plus continuous glucose monitoring data for type 1 diabetes.
Used 18 months of follow-up to predict outcomes at 24 months, citing evidence and auditing its reasoning.
evidence_signal: Pooled AUROC was 0.815 versus 0.656–0.700 for comparators in type 2 diabetes and 0.756 versus 0.603–0.631 in type 1 diabetes; only 4 of 70,246 cited values mismatched the chart.
watch_item: The abstract does not report external validation or prospective clinical impact, leaving generalizability and real-world benefit uncertain.
paper_title: Agentic LLM reasoning in pediatric diabetes outcome prediction from multimodal medical records
